entries.title: Background
entries.content: For nearly two weeks after the Supreme Court temporarily suspended the quota ruling on 10 July 2024, the protests had remained largely peaceful, even as the “Bangla Blockade” standoff continued. On 15 July 2024, that changed. Across multiple universities, groups affiliated with the ruling party's student wing — the Bangladesh Chhatra League — attacked quota-reform protesters on their own campuses. At Dhaka University, clashes with unarmed demonstrators reportedly lasted nearly five hours; reports put the number of injured at over 300, with separate police figures cited in the same coverage placing the count of those treated at Dhaka Medical College Hospital near 297. The figures are approximate and vary by source. Many of the attackers reportedly came from outside the university, armed with sticks and iron rods, and female students were beaten in full view of onlookers. Police fired rubber bullets and tear gas to disperse protesters at the campus sites.

entries.title: What Followed
entries.content: On the evening of 15 July 2024, BCL activists reportedly stormed the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, disrupting treatment for the wounded. On the same day, a separate BCL attack was reported at Jahangirnagar University, reportedly led by that campus's own BCL branch president, and attacks were also reported at Rajshahi University, Chittagong University, Jagannath University, and Eden Mohila College. The same day's reports describe a coordinated or near-simultaneous set of attacks on quota-reform protesters at multiple university campuses around the country, not a single isolated incident. The violence on 15 July 2024 marked a turning point and is the starting point for the next phase of the movement, covered in later chapters.
